arguments.literal: Class -> re-enters at; flows through: goal_reprice (current bounded work-wave focus changes) -> Goals; Intent, Product, Requirements, Design, Code and Evidence where that focus changes deeper constitutional truth. intent_reprice (directional or scope change) -> Intent; Product, Requirements, Design, Code, Evidence. product_reprice (current product realisation changes while directional intent stays stable) -> Product; Requirements, Design, Code, Evidence. requirement_reprice (constitutional truth changes while project direction stays stable) -> Requirements; Design, Code, Evidence. design_reframe (realisation structure changes while active intent and requirement truth stay stable) -> Design; Code, Evidence. realization_refactor (local code, configuration or attribute change with no intended constitutional or structural change) -> the realised surface only; nothing upstream, and it must prove no upstream drift.
A closed result is reused by an unchanged consumer that checks exact applicability; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates nothing.

For one governed boundary B, M(B) = entities + identities + relationships + cardinalities + invariants + authorities + authority transitions + functions + higher-order composition laws + topology + lifecycle states and transitions + public contracts + externally observable Product meaning + declared domains and admission conditions + failure and refusal routes + effect and closure laws + projections + module mappings + material algorithmic obligations; U(B) = unresolved(M(B)). B is decision-complete when U(B) is empty, M(B) forms one jointly satisfiable constraint network, and every network admitted by M(B) is semantically equivalent under the governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations. This is the design gate's acceptance criterion: a boundary is ready for retained implementation without a prior gate exactly when it is decision-complete, and a gate that cannot reach decision completeness has not closed.
DESIGN_MODULE §5 Decision-complete symbolic design; P1, P2, P6

Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary carries one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view Mermaid design asset before the boundary is promoted or claims design-method closure. When co_evolution_admissible(B) holds, design evidence, implementation and tests may develop together before that gate; otherwise the affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation is accepted before retained implementation establishes it. Unchanged boundaries cite their accepted basis; local realisation work with no material semantic-boundary delta does not recreate this gate. The asset contains a Mermaid classDiagram domain model, a sequenceDiagram execution model and a stateDiagram-v2 lifecycle model; another text-native format is lawful only when ratified and preserving the same three views and cross-view checks; one broad flowchart does not substitute. The views may be sections of one design surface sharing one acceptance decision (no three files, tickets, reviews or ceremonies); they are fidelity-checked projections of the accepted Ontology, not peer truth surfaces.
DESIGN_MODULE §7 Ontology and three-view design gate; P1, P2, P6

For a new or semantically changed boundary, the Ontology and design verdict are both accepted before the affected implementation, public contract or semantic carrier is promoted or the work claims design-method closure. Any failed applicable axiom, missing functionality disposition, unresolved authority path or blocking realisation gap keeps the verdict non-accepted. If the Ontology, any of the three views, the cross-view evaluation or either accepted verdict is absent, the boundary is not design-method complete; work may continue as provisional co-evolution only when co_evolution_admissible(B) holds, and the affected boundary may not be promoted, published or closed. The asset stays boundary-bounded: mixing an active semantic boundary with unrelated bootstrap, test-harness, projection or delivery shapes to look complete is a defect.
DESIGN_MODULE §7 Gate and retrospective work; P2, P6

The selected relation and its basis belong in the existing work or design carrier; no separate artifact is required. If implementation exposes previously hidden architectural ambiguity, the boundary switches to design-gated sequencing at the smallest causally closed affected decision set rather than retroactively invalidating unrelated work. Serial implementation repairs do not establish design acceptance. Repeated or cross-cutting material surprises are evidence that the affected design cut is underconstrained and require one bounded design_reframe (SPEC_METHOD §4 Change classes); retained code remains provisional evidence until that reframe is accepted.
DESIGN_MODULE §5 Proportional design sequencing; SPEC_METHOD §4 Change classes; P2, P6

The bidirectional design-and-implementation relation is an evidence relation, not bidirectional semantic authority. Implementation may provide a counterexample, falsify a constraint or expose hidden ambiguity. It may not select the missing semantic answer, rewrite upstream truth to legalise itself, or ratify a material design decision after establishing it.
DESIGN_MODULE §5 Proportional design sequencing; P6

When co_evolution_admissible(B) holds, implementation may precede or develop with design evidence and may be retained after reconciliation; until the design gate is accepted it is provisional evidence: it does not author semantic truth, earn publication authority, or satisfy promotion or closure. Otherwise only a disposable spike may cross the affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation before design acceptance. Existing implementation under retrospective review may inform the affected design; newly discovered material ambiguity, contradiction or a materially non-equivalent network makes decision_complete(B) false and activates the design gate for that decision. Promotion and design-method closure stay blocked until the Ontology, three-view asset and axiom evaluation are accepted. The design evaluates the code against prior authority; it does not rewrite the Ontology or diagrams to rationalise an unlawful implementation shape.
DESIGN_MODULE §7 Gate and retrospective work; P2, P6

At a material semantic boundary, Prime contraction applies to each candidate semantic atom and then to the complete family those contractions produce. A locally irreducible atom is not globally Prime when the family duplicates identity, authority, function, lifecycle, topology, effect or projection meaning; local Prime-conformance of realisation units does not prove the family globally Prime. Contraction preserves root authority and every retained semantic relation; reducing files, functions, operations or authoring surfaces cannot compensate for introducing another authority source or truth path. Prime evidence states the complete candidate semantic-atom family; each atom's stable identity, irreducible relation, admitted domain and falsification condition; the whole-family contraction relation; retained meaning and authority before and after contraction; accepted loss; and the explicit total mapping from every proposed realisation projection to its accepted atom or atoms. Work inside an accepted boundary cites the existing Prime basis rather than recreating it.
DESIGN_MODULE §5 Recursive Prime and root conservation (UP-003); FOUNDATIONS §4 Conservation accounting; P2, P3, P4b, P6

Ontology, Prime contraction, IACS, target design, the domain, sequence and state views, public contracts, module boundaries, implementation and tests are projections of one network; their presence, section names, individual plausibility or mechanical validity does not establish decision completeness. The boundary is underconstrained whenever decision_complete(B) is false, including when implementation has to introduce a new material semantic decision, projections contradict one another, or two materially non-equivalent networks remain admissible. Local algorithm and layout choices may remain open only when every admitted choice is semantically equivalent under the accepted network. Contradictory projections make the design unsatisfiable and block promotion. Decision completeness requires no further document when existing Ontology, algebra, module mapping and views jointly carry the complete relation.
DESIGN_MODULE §5 Decision-complete symbolic design; P1, P2, P5; EVALUATION §1

co_evolution_admissible(B) iff decision_complete(B); design_gate(B) = the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish decision_complete(B). Design sequencing follows decision_complete(B), not one global authoring order. Co-evolution is lawful only when decision_complete(B) holds: design still owns the structural HOW, but design, implementation and tests may evolve together and reconcile before promotion or closure. Design-gated sequencing is required when implementation would otherwise establish an unresolved or contradictory relation, or choose between materially non-equivalent networks, with durable consequences for future change: the affected design decision is accepted before retained implementation establishes it. A disposable spike may supply evidence without becoming the selected design.
DESIGN_MODULE §5 Proportional design sequencing; P0, P2, P6

Neither mode is the global default; the same proportionality relation selects between them. Proportionality decides which relations are material and bounds the smallest affected gate; decision completeness is the resulting admissibility test. Where a bounded symbolic model can contract the material semantic alternatives within effective reasoning capacity, the code, runtime-state, test, review and reconciliation space it removes is counterfactual evidence of that contraction, not an independent reason for a design gate. A prior design gate is warranted when it removes material semantic ambiguity whose alternatives would establish materially different durable architecture and that contraction justifies its reasoning load; it is disproportionate when upstream truth leaves no materially divergent architecture to adjudicate and a separate prior acceptance would add no disambiguation. Design still records and owns the resulting HOW before promotion or closure.
DESIGN_MODULE §5 Proportional design sequencing; ACTIVATION §6; P2, P6

A semantically coherent design is not acceptable when its selected substrate cannot natively construct the required identities, relationships, transitions, authority boundaries, effects, lifecycle, composition, publication and retirement behaviour. A missing substrate capability remains an explicit design gap or triggers lawful re-entry (SPEC_METHOD §4); it is not hidden behind a reference bridge, adapter, filesystem runner, test double or promised future feature (SPEC_METHOD §7 Bridge prohibition). This is a constructability obligation, not a prescribed implementation; the consumer chooses the substrate and the evidence mechanism.
DESIGN_MODULE §5 Native constructability (UP-002); P0, P2, P5, P6

For an unchanged realization_refactor, the gate is proportional: cite the accepted Ontology and design basis, identify the touched projection set, and prove that entities, relationships, lifecycle, authority, functions, effects and public semantics have no delta. That proof reuses the existing verdict; it does not create a new Ontology or acceptance ceremony.
DESIGN_MODULE §7 Gate and retrospective work; ACTIVATION §7; P2
An obligation with no route to the selected outcome is unjustified.
A selected outcome defines adequacy; interfaces inherit material obligations from the transformation they serve.
Standing: independent. Identical capacity serves opposite purposes.

Proportionality is the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and effective reasoning complexity introduced. A method obligation is proportional when its contraction of the admissible interpretation space justifies the additional concepts, relations, projections and evidence an actor must hold together to reach a correct decision.

Every substantive change, whatever its intake label, enters through one intake triage that names the smallest lawful re-entry point; triage records the change intent, the class, the re-entry point and when triage occurred, wherever substantive work begins.
Every transformation records what it preserved, introduced and removed, its external resolution witnesses and its residuals.

frame_indexes.scope: Decide one design boundary's sequencing and gate: the decision-complete criterion over the complete material-relation set, co-evolution versus design-gated sequencing selected by proportionality, implementation as evidence not authority, native constructability (UP-002), recursive Prime and root conservation (UP-003), and the Ontology and three-view gate with its verdicts, the unchanged-refactor reuse and provisional pre-gate implementation. Selected for F-03 task D.

residuals.detail: PROFILES section 3 conserves DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD by reference, which requires the ontology-first derivation chain where it applies, while ACTIVATION section 6 asks every obligation to pay for the ambiguity it removes. Whether a design boundary with no material alternative must still pay the full chain is not decided by this corpus; it is a question for the profile's owner.

Each independent commitment carries a one-sentence non-entailment argument in its qualification. These are claims of independence with an informal witness each; none is formalised and P4a states none. The accepted C1 realisation argues them at greater length; the standard conserves only the sentence.

symbols.label: Applicability check: the check an unchanged consumer performs before reusing a closed result
Change class: goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice, design_reframe or realization_refactor, each with its re-entry point

Closed result: identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual uncertainty and the invalidation conditions; minimal shape REFERENCE_FRAME section 13; available for reuse under an applicability check
Transformation record: preserved, introduced, removed, external resolution witnesses, residuals
The chain Goals, Intent, Product Definition, Requirements, Design and realisation, Code or documents, Events, Projection, Delta, Scenarios, Gap analysis, Repricing
Decision complete: U(B) is empty, M(B) is jointly satisfiable, and every network M(B) admits is semantically equivalent under the governing Product, requirements and accepted design
Disposable spike: implementation that supplies evidence without becoming the selected design or retained implementation
Design gate: the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish decision completeness, closed by an accepted Ontology, a complete three-view asset and accepted axiom evaluation
Governed design boundary B: one boundary whose complete material-relation set M(B) and unresolved members U(B) decide its design sequencing and gate
Complete material-relation set M(B): every material relation of boundary B, from entities and identities to module mappings and material algorithmic obligations
UP-002 Native constructability: the selected substrate natively constructs every required design relation
Ontology and design verdict: the two acceptances (accepted or non-accepted) a new or semantically changed boundary needs before promotion or design-method closure
UP-003 Recursive Prime and root conservation: Prime contraction over each atom and the whole family, preserving root authority
Design sequencing mode: co-evolution (design, implementation and tests evolve together) or design-gated sequencing (the affected decision is accepted before retained implementation establishes it)
Three-view design asset: Mermaid classDiagram domain model, sequenceDiagram execution model and stateDiagram-v2 lifecycle model, fidelity-checked projections of the accepted Ontology
P1 Interpretation
P2 Purpose
P3 Identity
P4a Typed composition
P6 Justification and authority
Promotion: an explicit relation between an unchanged subject and its admission or acceptance judgment
Proportionality: the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and effective reasoning complexity introduced
Software design profile: binds the ontology-first derivation chain and the design laws
Intake triage: change intent, class, re-entry point and when triage occurred
